extracted.intended_audience: readers of early modern voyage narratives; historians and students of exploration/colonial history
extracted.subtask_description: A primary-source chapter from an early 17th-century Spanish voyage describing encounters with natives, ceremonial possession of land, military organisation, municipal foundation, and feast celebrations. Useful for scholars of exploration, colonial ritual, and maritime history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for zeal, management, and intelligible communication in native encounters
rubrics_metrics.description: On such occasions 'it is a great evil, on such occasions, when there is a want of zeal or of management.' There was no one who could make himself intelligible; the lack of understanding and poor management led to panic and violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure effective communication (interpreters or gestures), maintain discipline among troops (avoid impatience or forgetting orders), avoid provocative actions (firing low), and prevent mishandling of casualties that might inflame relations (the account shows that displaying a mutilated comrade led chiefs to withdraw and later attack).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of cruel provocation and enforcement of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: An undisciplined soldier fired low and killed a native; a drummer mutilated the body, and officers who showed the corpse to chiefs 'pretending that this cruelty was a means of making peace' precipitated hostilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not employ gratuitous cruelty or public mutilation as a negotiation tactic; enforce orders and restrain soldiers to prevent isolated violent acts that can transform contact into war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of a ministry of war and marine (administrative requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: It was 'very necessary and obligatory to create a ministry of war and marine' so that by land and sea there might be established order for security, discipline, union of wills, defence of roads, escorts, and ambuscades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an organized command structure with named officers (Admiral, Master of the Camp, Royal Ensign, Sergeant-Major, Captains, artillery captain, constables, pilots, etc.) to ensure defence, logistics, discipline, and royal authority; appoint officers with clear roles to avoid ad hoc command failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding a chivalric order / insignia to bind settlers (Knights of the Holy Ghost)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Captain announced an Order titled 'Knights of the Holy Ghost,' gave a blue cross as insignia, sought free consent, and set obligations, promises of privileges, and spiritual/legal backing from Pope and King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symbolic insignia and formal vows/constitutions to bind settlers to duties; obtain ecclesiastical/royal approval where relevant; accompany such foundations with confession and religious observance to legitimize and morally integrate participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for taking possession (Raising of the Cross & formal proclamations)
rubrics_metrics.description: To take possession: plant/raise a cross, have clergy receive it, proceed to a pedestal and 'plant' the cross, and have the secretary read formal possessions—six set proclamations (in the name of the Trinity; the Catholic Church; St. Francis; John of God; the Order of the Holy Ghost; and His Majesty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a ritualized sequence—public ceremonial planting of the cross, liturgical acclamations, and loud public reading of formulas claiming the land in specific religious and royal names—to create a clear record of possession and invoke ecclesiastical and sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial liturgy and procession order for major festivals (Pentecost / Corpus Christi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed festival practices: erect a booth/altar ('Our Lady of Loreto'), display lights and artillery, music, rockets; order of procession (soldier with heavy cross, lay brother with gilt cross, acolytes, three companies with banners and drums, sword-dance and other dances, royal standard accompanied by officers, magistrates with torches, Commissary with pall borne by officers, priests carrying the sacrament).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure public religious celebrations with theatrical and military elements to assert presence and authority: set up a chapel/altar, organize processional order, include local entertainment adapted to troupe, use salutes (muskets, artillery) and visible insignia to signal power and piety; integrate manumission or public rewards into festivals as moral/political acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding municipal government: election and oath-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: After taking possession the Captain 'would elect a municipality and such officers as is usual in a city'; elections were agreed and officers (magistrates, secretary, justices, chief constable, royal officers such as accountant, treasurer, factor, registrar of mines, store-keeper, overseer) were named and took an oath placing the right hand on a breviary held by the Father Commissary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When establishing a settlement, hold formal elections of local magistrates and officers, require a sworn oath of loyalty placed on a religious text, and publicly record appointments to confer legitimacy and continuity of royal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manumission and public acts of charity as part of ceremonial observance
rubrics_metrics.description: During the festivities the Captain asked officers to free two slaves; letters were drawn up and the slaves were manumitted 'by reason of pious motives and of the honour of the festival of that day.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public festivals to perform notable acts (manumission, charitable deeds) that convey moral legitimacy and reinforce the expedition's piety and benevolence to observers and to the Crown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural establishment and provisioning as a settlement strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Captain sowed seeds (maize, cotton, onions, melons, pumpkins, beans, pulse) to establish food sources; parties foraging inland collected roots, fish, and livestock (pigs, hens) to provision the ships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize sowing familiar crops and systematic foraging/fishing to create local provisions; balance short-term foraging (capturing livestock or collecting fish) with long-term planting to sustain expeditions and future settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Armed reconnaissance and combined ship–shore combat tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Landing parties were formed in squadrons and ambushes deployed; when surrounded or attacked, supporting parties were landed and ship artillery (guns, bombards) and shore batteries were fired to break enemy positions and cover retreats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct reconnaissance in force with scouts/spies posted; maintain reserves to support threatened detachments; use naval gunfire and shore pieces to disrupt enemy concentrations and protect withdrawal; coordinate between ship and land forces to preserve spoils and personnel.
